info.title: Job Finder API
info.description: Job search / scoring / auto-apply pipeline as an API. Every field that used to live in a hardcoded config.py (keywords, locations, skills, resume, applicant info, ATS targets, thresholds) is now part of the request body, so a frontend can drive the whole pipeline dynamically.

post.description:
Kicks off a job search across LinkedIn/Indeed/Naukri on the Celery
"default" queue (this can take minutes due to rate-limit pacing — any
available "default"-queue worker process can pick it up). Poll
GET /tasks/{task_id} for status and the resulting job list.

Fetches jobs from Greenhouse/Lever/SmartRecruiters/Workday, or a
custom company career page.

For platform="custom": the worker first tries a plain JSON API probe
against custom_endpoint_url. If that returns nothing usable (common
for JS-rendered career sites, e.g. SuccessFactors-based boards), it
falls back to a headless-Playwright DOM scrape — but only if you also
supply custom_list_selector (and optionally custom_title_selector /
custom_link_selector / custom_location_selector). Without selectors,
an unscrapeable custom page fails loudly with a message telling you
what to inspect, rather than silently returning zero jobs.

Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} for status and results.

Kicks off LLM-based job scoring (keyword pre-filter -> Gemini ->
Groq -> HF fallback) on the Celery "default" queue. Poll
GET /tasks/{task_id} for status and the ranked job list.

Deprecated (P4b): use POST /apply/runs. Kept for one release.

Opens top-matched jobs in a real Playwright browser on the Celery
worker and pre-fills LinkedIn Easy Apply forms — never auto-submits.
Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} for status, and GET /applications for the
tracked application rows (scoped to your account).

NOTE: a client-supplied browser_profile_dir is ignored — see
build_apply_params.

Returns the ready pack (200) or starts building one (202; poll
GET /apply/prep/{id}). A ready pack is reused until your master resume
changes or `regenerate` is true. Asking for nothing (both false) still
gives the email draft.

Preflight (switches, level, risk notice, caps, duplicates, company
cooldown, resume) and a queued run; a worker on the apply queue opens
the form next. Nothing is submitted until you approve the run.

get.description: state: a run state, or `waiting` (needs you). job_id: the runs for one job (newest first).

schema.title: Response List Proofs Api V1 Apply Runs  Run Id  Proofs Get

post.description:
Fan-out version: dispatches one search+score sub-task PER KEYWORD
in parallel (Celery group), each pushing scored jobs to Redis the
instant they're ready. Returns immediately with a run_id — poll
GET /pipeline/{run_id}/jobs to watch results arrive live, and
GET /pipeline/{run_id} for run-level progress (X/Y keywords done).

Each job appears once per run. If a better copy of a job already in the
feed turns up later (LinkedIn over Indeed), an updated entry with the
SAME `id` and `replaces: true` is appended — upsert entries by `id`.

get.description:
The newest search you started on Jobs, while the server still holds
its results (6 h): run meta plus `created_at`, `keywords` and
`skipped_sources`. Load its jobs with GET /pipeline/{run_id}/jobs?offset=0.
404 when there is none. Job-alert runs are not included.

post.description:
Stops a streaming run: keyword tasks that haven't started skip their
work; jobs already in the feed stay. Idempotent.

get.description:
Poll this every ~2s, passing `offset` = the previous response's
`next_offset`, to fetch only the NEW entries each tick. An entry whose
`id` you already have (`replaces: true`) is a better copy of that job:
replace it in place.

post.description:
Runs search -> score -> (optional) apply as a single Celery task.
Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} for status and the combined result.

Emails a 6-digit code. The response is identical whether or not the
address has (or may create) an account.
Lets an OTP/Google user add a password (or change their own).

Exchanges the refresh cookie for a new access token (and a new
refresh cookie). Call with credentials included.

"Apply manually → Mark as applied" (CLAUDE.md 7.7): the user applied
on the job's own page (`submitted`) or sent the Email apply draft
(`emailed`, P4a). Recorded with status_source `manual`; the job moves
to the user's Applied list so later searches skip it.

Adds a model from any supported provider. Once enabled, every user
sees it in GET /models (free ones are usable by everyone at once).

To hide it temporarily, PATCH enabled_global=false instead.

post.description:
Adds (or replaces) your key for one scope. Models and job sources
with that scope use it for your requests; it is never shown again.

Stores a new version (the first one becomes the master). With
`parse` (default), a worker reads it with AI: poll GET /resumes/{id}
until `parse_status` leaves "pending", then let the user review and
save it with PUT /resumes/{id}.

Reads the resume again with AI. Replaces the parsed profile when it
finishes (including edits saved earlier).

A new profile with the skills and recent titles from a parsed resume
(the master by default). Weights start as "strong"; edit them after.

Adjacent job titles from the profile's skills (AI). Nothing is saved:
the user picks which to add.

risk_notice.title: Risk Notice
risk_notice.default: Auto apply fills and submits applications on company career sites (Greenhouse, Lever) for you, only after you review and approve each one. Some sites limit automated applications, answers can still be wrong, and a submitted application can't be taken back. You stay responsible for every application sent in your name. LinkedIn applications are never submitted by the app.

generic_notice.title: Generic Notice
generic_notice.default: The AI form reader (beta) fills application forms on other career sites (Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Workable and more). It is less reliable than the Greenhouse and Lever support: it can misread a question or a page. It never signs in or creates accounts, every application waits for your review, and pages it can't handle are handed back to you. It may use a paid image-reading AI model for hard pages, within a per-application limit.

PipelineRequest.title: PipelineRequest
PipelineRequest.description:
Two ways to describe what to look for (CLAUDE.md 7.3):

- **search_profile_id** (preferred): keywords, skills, must/nice/exclude
  terms come from the saved Keywords & Skills profile; the resume context
  from the master resume (or `score.resume_summary`); locations and
  posted-within from the user's preferences unless `search` sets them.
- **legacy**: `search.keywords` + `score` (resume_summary, skills, …) sent
  every time. Still works; deprecated once the frontend uses profiles.

Either way, jobs the user has already seen, hidden or applied to are
skipped (`include_seen: true` shows seen/saved ones again), avoided
companies are dropped, and each job is scored once per run.

`career_targets` come from the profile and only `resume_summary`, the
thresholds and one-run keys here are used.
